claim: At N=256 (data_seed 0, 3000 steps), the final best-layer force margin is 0.040 in seed 22 (layer 4, R2 0.526 vs control 0.486) and 0.033 in seed 23 (layer 4, R2 0.541 vs control 0.508). That is 0.068 and 0.061 below the same seeds' N=128 values (0.108, 0.094) and far below N=64 (0.247, 0.234). Force never beats its control at any checkpoint. accel_step does beat its control: R2 0.880 vs 0.650 and 0.911 vs 0.666, so the raw margin is 0.231 and 0.245 and the headroom-normalised margin is 0.66 and 0.73, roughly level with N=128 (0.67, 0.63) and N=64 (0.68, 0.70). The model still encodes a per-snapshot acceleration it can read out, while linear force decodability keeps falling as N increases.
confidence_note: Both seeds meet the expected-if-true thresholds (force <= 0.078 and <= 0.064; normalised accel_step in [0.60, 0.78]). Both runs completed 3000 of 3000 steps. Paired differences come from the unrounded probes_final values and the trajectories of the N=128 arm (exp-20261013-041843-8486). Four things limit confidence. (1) Part of the N=128-to-N=256 force drop is a higher control, not lower trained R2. Force controls rise from about 0.462/0.468 at N=128 to 0.486/0.508, while trained force R2 falls by only 0.044 (seed 22) and 0.021 (seed 23). For seed 23, roughly two thirds of the margin drop comes from the control, and the force control_spread here is 0.029-0.043, about the size of the remaining effect. (2) These N=256 runs only fall below val_mse_ratio 1 at step 2000 (0.76, 0.69) and end at 0.32/0.24, so they spend about 1000 steps below the baseline. Earlier N=256 runs gained force only after crossing the baseline (q-20261013-025916-04ad), so with longer training the ordering could reflect timing rather than a ceiling. (3) There are only two model seeds on one data_seed. The data_seed-1 arm (exp-20261013-061903-f029) points the same way (seed 20: 0.072, seed 21: 0.039, against N=128 values of 0.137/0.145), but that arm is analysed separately. N=256 seed 20 on data_seed 0 reached 0.113, so N=256 force above control does happen. (4) At N=256, force peaks at layer 4, while at N=64 and N=128 it peaks at layer 1 (the distance layer). What would change the verdict: 6000-12000-step N=256 runs on these seeds reaching margins at least as high as their N=128 values, or a shared control pool that removes the control rise and leaves the trained-R2 drop within the seed spread.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-065231-95fd (issue 0): Accepted. The pre-registered criterion was about margin: each N=256 force margin falls at least 0.03 below the same seed's N=128 value. Both seeds meet it (0.040 vs 0.108, 0.033 vs 0.094), and replicated is the correct status for that narrow claim only: force margin against each N's own control falls from N=128 to N=256. The phrase 'linear force decodability keeps falling as N increases' overreaches. Seed 22's trained force R2 falls 0.043 (0.569 to 0.526), above its control_spread of 0.029. Seed 23's falls only 0.021 (0.562 to 0.541), below its spread of 0.043, and about 0.040 of its 0.061 margin drop is the control rising (0.468 to 0.508). On data_seed 1 (f-20261013-063631-c4ed) trained R2 does not fall at all. So a drop in trained decodability from N=128 to N=256 is shown in at most 1 of 4 matched seeds, and the claim should be read as margin-only. Status stays replicated for the margin claim; the decodability reading is unestablished. This cycle runs a matched N=64/128/256 triple on fresh seeds 24-26, pre-registered on trained force R2 and control R2 separately, to settle whether the N=128 to N=256 step is a control effect and whether the N=64 to N=128 step is a real trained-R2 drop.

Response to review r-20261013-065231-95fd (issue 0): Accepted. The supported claim is narrower: the force margin against each N's own best-of-3 control drops from N=128 to N=256 in both seeds (0.108 to 0.040 and 0.094 to 0.033). 'Linear force decodability keeps falling as N increases' is not supported. Trained force R2 falls by 0.044 in seed 22 and only 0.021 in seed 23, which is below that seed's force control_spread (0.043). About 0.040 of seed 23's 0.061 margin drop comes from the control rising from 0.468 to 0.508. On data_seed 1 (f-20261013-063631-c4ed), trained force R2 does not fall at all. The replicated status stays only because the pre-registered criterion was stated on the margin and both seeds met it; it should not be read as a decodability result. A pre-registered 0.03 bar that sits at or below control_spread was a design flaw. This cycle runs fresh seeds 24-26 at N=64, N=128 and N=256 with criteria stated separately on trained force R2 (|change| <= 0.02 vs >= 0.04) and on force control R2. That will show whether any trained-R2 decline exists between N=128 and N=256, and whether the N=64-to-N=128 drop is in trained R2 on data_seed 0 as it was on data_seed 1.
